topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's place in the course and introduces its aims without yet developing the substantive material.

topics.label: Molecular changes driving cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how changes in a cell's molecular state can enable tumor development beyond a strictly ordered accumulation of mutations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy influences its capacity to initiate or propagate a tumor.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness as a promoter of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that enable previously nonmalignant mutant cells to form tumors.

topics.label: Stromal dependence of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive stromal cells as a basis for targeting the tumor microenvironment therapeutically.

topics.label: Investigating cancer with single-cell and spatial omics
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular profiling of tissue specimens can reveal tumor evolution and interactions between cells.

topics.label: An integrated account of cancer evolution and susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes cancer development as the convergence of favorable cellular and environmental conditions, extending that account to developmental susceptibility in childhood.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming discussion of therapy.
